implementation.engine: four Rust crates; independent length-framed application IPC and NUL-framed JSON Chromium pipes
implementation.residentRuntime: Shared five-source manifest includes codec, evaluation, pinned selector bundle, condition registry and locator wrapper; Rust, JavaScript and tests verify the same length-framed source hash.
implementation.ownership: Independent guardian owns the browser process group and profile. A group-exit barrier keeps the leader unreaped until every member stops. Shared shutdown completion never kills the guardian for slow profile cleanup; bounded operation cleanup reports guardianContinuingCleanup when necessary.
implementation.cancellation: withdraw queued allocation, consume dispatched allocation reply then dispose, close owned browser when allocation result cannot be recovered, dispose success arriving after caller deadline
implementation.cleanupMetadata: error details identify resource disposal, undispatched work or browser-shutdown fallback
implementation.navigation: Loader-aware event state retains bounded completion records. Received-event acknowledgement barriers synchronize input completion with navigation state; document commits detach the old child-frame subtree even if Chromium omits individual detach events.
implementation.locator: One isolated runtime per frame document with shared initialization and execution-time membership; ordinary locator operations retain host deadlines and retries, while opt-in assertions register exact-context resident conditions.
implementation.input: Native text and pointer input with method-specific actionability, fresh frame stability, hit interception, button/modifier cleanup and navigation barriers. Protocol results and errors carry operation input delivery progress, including replies crossing the caller deadline. Keyboard, pointer and fill/focus mutations share per-page input ownership. Key chords are validated before effects; interrupted keys are released or the affected page is closed. Pinned macOS editing commands preserve platform shortcuts. Page-level presses retain current focus and use an unbounded operation without locator navigation waiting. Undelayed clicks admit their whole bounded command sequence atomically, dispatch in wire order without reply barriers, and withdraw unsent commands on cancellation. Uncertain pointer delivery closes the owned page without replaying a release; the input lock remains held through disposal.
implementation.rendererExpiry: Wall-clock renderer guard suppresses already-expired work queued behind a blocked event loop; the Rust monotonic deadline remains authoritative.
implementation.assertions: Complete pinned predicates and bounded observations in both host-polled and opt-in resident paths. Authoritative host monotonic deadlines cannot accept late success. Responsive cancellation gathers terminal diagnostics; blocked-renderer cancellation retains bounded exact-context cleanup until acknowledgement or owner closure.
implementation.runner: Pinned flashwright-upstream-runner alias supplies scheduling and generic assertion infrastructure; _baseTest is the private boundary. Native fixtures and expect.extend browser matchers dispatch only to Flashwright. Plain library loading is independent of the scheduler.
implementation.handshake: The client requires every implemented operation capability before dispatching browser allocation; missing keyboard.press is covered by a rejecting fake-driver test.
implementation.evaluationErrors: Explicit execution/argument-decoding/result-serialization stages with private codec error identity and independently bounded UTF-16 diagnostics; Node argument encoding uses the same classification.
implementation.launchPolicy: Default CDP Chromium arguments extracted from the pinned reference, including default headed/headless variants; the guardian substitutes its owned profile at the retained position. Shared benchmark contracts compare actual emitted launch arguments.
implementation.pageFocusPolicy: Main page sessions enable Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled, matching pinned Playwright initialization. Two-page visibility/focus and fresh pointer-frame checks conform; a blocked handler in one page leaves another page usable.
implementation.testFailureCleanup: Unittest cleanup registered immediately after owner creation; only the worker/driver is terminated, and guardian completion is awaited before diagnostic streams close. Four intentionally failed setup/body cases cover both owner paths.
implementation.protocolAttribution: Opt-in external byte-preserving Chromium pipe proxy records bounded command metadata and script hashes without argument/result payloads. Two clock calibrations bound Node/Python epoch offset, and an independent verifier recomputes correlated phase accounting. Instrumented timing is diagnostic only.
implementation.residentRegistryExperiment: Default-off fair registry with synchronous selector sharing, coalesced timer groups and indexed document CSS lookup. Current 104-group conformance, Node22 checks and 57 registry cases pass. All 210 ordinary launches independently verify; every CPU/memory/time load gate passes. Complete-flow comparisons improve time by about 5.5% and 6.7%, below the material target: compatibility/evidence/resident-indexed-performance-checkpoint-2026-10-08.json
implementation.ordinaryResourceClose: Ordinary page/context closure waits for its actual Chromium acknowledgement. The bounded operation-cancellation disposal budget no longer causes a slow ordinary close to shut down the entire browser. Unit test withholds close acknowledgement for 750ms; full emulated Linux suite passes.
implementation.benchmarkBrowserBinding: Core reports bind exact browser path, SHA-256, version and distribution; new benchmark admission and independent verification require that identity. compatibility/evidence/browser-distribution-checkpoint-2026-10-07.json
implementation.runtimeSourceEncoding: Resident source files remain ASCII, enforced by the Rust build. Unicode runtime values use JavaScript escapes without changing diagnostics or supported application text. A literal U+2026 caused a verified installation regression; compatibility/evidence/ascii-runtime-checkpoint-2026-10-07.json
implementation.residentResourceMeasurement: Fixed-work sustained-load harness covers quiet text, property-only and mutation workloads at 1/32/128 conditions with all six engine orders, actual launch flags, backend/application counts, source/browser/binary binding and self-contained verification logs. Corrected CPU accounting survives macOS zombie resets. compatibility/evidence/resident-load-checkpoint-2026-10-08.json

limitations: No platform runtime publication or automatic driver acquisition; npm consumers provide an explicit compiled driver path
No complete runner adapter, aliases, pnpm or Yarn verification yet
Value coverage is a tested development subset, not full differential conformance with every Playwright evaluation case

Two current matched headless-shell Playwright comparisons show paired complete-run ratios 1.1303 (1.0547–1.1719) and 1.0515 (1.0090–1.0734), about 11.5% and 4.9% less time respectively. Delayed assertion ratios are 2.420 and 2.394. Only the first snapshot passes the configured 10% material threshold; the larger setup advantage did not repeat. Noop/failure median regressions remain in both; the replication also flags noop/assertion observed maxima. The material target remains open. Residency stays opt-in, with broader release gates still open.
Emulated Linux functional evidence does not satisfy native Linux performance gates
Navigation/network support is the tested development subset; URLPattern, full header/cookie variants, routing, API requests and service-worker semantics require further conformance
Screenshot artifacts remain unimplemented; persistent Page.keyboard down/up, sequential typing and broader keyboard APIs remain unimplemented
Cross-process child-frame routing explicitly rejects; FrameLocator, handles and broader frame/navigation conformance remain unfinished
Native text input containing unpaired UTF-16 surrogates rejects explicitly; selector and read strings preserve those units
Locator coverage is an experimental tested subset; complete option/export enforcement and adversarial input/cancellation conformance remain release gates
TodoMVC migration verification uses the public demo URL retained by the original fixture; asset hashes are checked before and after but offline application reproduction is not yet available

Resident assertions remain opt-in. The current six-group matrix passes all CPU, memory and time gates. Two complete-flow replications improve time by about 5.5% and 6.7%, below the 10% material target, with noop/failure median regressions. Native Linux, contention and broader release gates remain open.
